newsitem.title: USA: Nearly 200 Silicon Valley executives endorse Dole.
newsitem.headline: Nearly 200 Silicon Valley executives endorse Dole.

text.p: Nearly 200 Silicon Valley executives endorsed Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole Tuesday, saying his policies would be better for the high-tech region than those of President Clinton.

The executives' support is a boost for Dole, who is trailing Clinton in the polls. Clinton enjoyed strong support in the 1992 election in California's Silicon Valley, home to many leading high-technology companies.
Last month 75 Silicon Valley executives, including Apple co-founder Steve Jobs, endorsed Clinton for re-election.
T. J. Rodgers, chief executive officer of Cypress Semiconductor Corp., said the Silicon Valley executives were annoyed because "we keep getting misconstrued as supporting Bill Clinton."

Rodgers was one of several high-profile chief executives among the 198 business people, venture capitalists and lawyers announcing their support for Dole, the former Senate majority leader, and vice-presidential running mate Jack Kemp.

Others included Jerry Sanders of Advanced Micro Devices Inc., James Barksdale of Netscape Communications Corp., Scott McNealy of Sun Microsystems Inc., Gilbert Amelio of Apple Computer Inc. and Wilfred Corrigan of LSI Logic Corp..

In a release, the endorsers said that after reviewing the needs of the Silicon Valley economy, they agreed that "important features of the Dole agenda are far superior to those offered by the current administration."

They praised what they called Dole's consistent stand on the need for securities reform legislation and his proposed cuts in income tax and capital gains tax. They said they also liked Dole's commitment to economic growth and his belief in less government.
